               RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS’ OBJECTIONS TO
                  DIRECT TESTIMONY OF APRIL CIANO



TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

    COMES NOW, April Ciano (“Ciano”), Pro Se Intervenor, and files this
Response to Applicants’ Objections to Direct Testimony of April Ciano




                                                                     Page 1|6
                                 I. INTRODUCTION

Applicants objected to portions of my testimony relating to publicly available health and
safety materials concerning electromagnetic fields (“EMF”), including exhibits from the
World Health Organization (“WHO”), the National Cancer Institute (“NCI”), and the
International Agency for Research on Cancer (“IARC”).

I respectfully request that the Administrative Law Judges deny Applicants’ request to
strike these materials in their entirety. My testimony and exhibits were not offered to
establish scientific certainty or to present expert medical opinions. They were offered to
demonstrate the existence of legitimate and well-documented community concern
regarding the placement of a 765-kV transmission line near homes, schools, and families,
including my own.

Community values, environmental integrity, and residential impacts are factors the
Commission is required to consider under PURA § 37.056(c), and my testimony is
directed to those required routing criteria.

                                 II. BACKGROUND

My testimony is based on my personal knowledge as a landowner, resident, caregiver,
grandmother, and member of the Salado community directly affected by the proposed
transmission line route.

The proposed route would run in close proximity to my home and property where
multiple family members reside, including my husband, a disabled veteran with service
connected conditions including PTSD, tinnitus, and sleep apnea; my brother, who faces
significant medical challenges and is unable to work; and my grandchildren, who attend
middle school and high school within Salado ISD.

This matter is deeply personal to my family. Our home is not simply a piece of property
to us. It is the place where we have worked to create a peaceful and stable environment
for the people we love and care for every day. One of the reasons we chose to move to a
quieter rural area was to create some distance from the constant noise, stress, and pace of
more heavily developed areas.

My testimony describes the ways in which the proposed transmission line would affect
the use, enjoyment, and character of our home environment, including noise, visual
impacts, disruption, and the loss of the quiet rural setting we intentionally sought out. I
also expressed concern regarding the placement of large scale industrial infrastructure
near residential neighborhoods and schools where children spend a substantial portion of
their time.

My husband lives with PTSD, tinnitus, and sleep apnea, and maintaining a calm and
stable home environment is important to his overall health and quality of life. He works
from home daily, which means he spends the majority of his time within this
                                                                            Page 2|6
 environment. Because of that, persistent noise, disruption, construction activity, and
changes to the surrounding environment would not be something he could simply leave
behind at the end of the day.

 His tinnitus is persistent and affects him daily. Over the years, we have used things such
as window air conditioning units and other background noise to help mask the ringing
and humming that he experiences. He also works from home, making the quiet and
stability of our home environment especially important to his daily routine and ability to
focus.

After more than 34 years of marriage, it is my personal observation that ongoing noise,
disruption, poor sleep, can negatively affect his overall health which in return affects his
quality of life.

I have also personally experienced the effect that persistent electrical infrastructure noise
can have on daily life and sleep. While living near lower voltage power lines in Lake
Havasu, I experienced a constant humming noise at night that regularly interfered with
my ability to sleep. During that same period, the noise also disrupted my husband’s sleep
because of his sensitivity to those types of sounds. That experience left a lasting
impression on both of us regarding the importance of a quiet and stable home
environment.

My brother also lives on our property and faces ongoing medical challenges, including
liver and kidney issues, and he is currently being monitored for possible pancreatic
cancer. Due to these conditions, periods of stress, disruption, and poor sleep can be
especially difficult for him. Maintaining a peaceful and stable home environment is
therefore very important to his overall health and quality of life.

For both my husband and brother, prolonged stress, disruption, construction activity,
persistent industrial noise, and the loss of the peaceful environment we intentionally
sought out can negatively affect their health and overall quality of life.

The exhibits objected to by Applicants consist of publicly available materials from
recognized institutions discussing EMF classifications and public health concerns. These
materials were provided to explain the basis for my personal concern and the broader
community concern reflected throughout this docket, not to offer expert scientific
conclusions.




                                    III. RESPONSE

                                                                             Page 3|6
 A. Personal Testimony Is Proper Lay Testimony

My testimony regarding my family, property, home environment, and community
concerns is based on my own personal observations and first-hand knowledge. I am not
offering medical diagnoses, engineering calculations, or expert scientific opinions.

I may properly testify regarding:

   •   the effects this project would have on my family’s daily life and our use and
       enjoyment of our property;
   •   my concern for nearby schools that my grandchildren attend within Salado ISD;
       and
   •   my concern for the health, safety, and well-being of those living near the
       proposed route.

These are first-hand accounts of my own household and community, not hearsay and not
expert testimony.

B. Exhibits AC-2 Through AC-4 Were Offered to Demonstrate Community
Concern, Not Scientific Proof

Exhibits AC-2 through AC-4 were not offered to prove that EMF exposure causes disease
or injury. They were offered to show that major public health institutions such as WHO,
NCI, and IARC have publicly discussed and classified EMF-related concerns.

These materials:

   •   exist and are publicly available from recognized health institutions;
   •   are part of the information that residents like me encounter; and
   •   help explain why community members experience genuine anxiety about living
       near a 765-kV transmission line.

I am not asking the Commission to treat these materials as conclusive scientific proof. I
am asking that they be considered for the limited purpose of demonstrating that my
concern—and the concern of many others—is grounded in publicly available information
from recognized institutions. That concern is directly relevant to “community values” and
“residential and community impacts” under PURA § 37.056(c).

C. Schools, Prudent Avoidance, and Community Values

The proposed routing near Salado ISD schools means that children would spend large
portions of their developing years in proximity to this line. As a grandmother whose
grandchildren attend school in Salado ISD, my concern about placing 150- to 190-foot
steel lattice towers near schools is based on personal observation and community values,
not on scientific expertise.

                                                                          Page 4|6
 The Commission’s prudent avoidance policy exists precisely because the science is
uncertain, not because harm has been definitively proven. That policy recognizes that
routing decisions may properly consider public concern and uncertainty regarding
potential exposure near homes and schools. My testimony is directed to that concern and
to the values of the community where my family lives, works, and attends school.

D. Broader Community Concern Already in the Record

The breadth of opposition and participation in this docket demonstrates that my concern
is not isolated. More than 3,600 filings and numerous intervenors have expressed concern
about the placement of this transmission line near homes, schools, ranches, wildlife
habitat, and established communities.

Multiple elected officials and public representatives have filed correspondence in this
docket raising concerns about routing impacts, residential neighborhoods, schools, and
landowner rights (items 3,30,344, and others). Furthermore, the elected officials
representing the Salado area have specifically raised concerns about impacts to
residential neighborhoods, schools and landowner rights. I am not offering those filings
as proof of scientific harm, but as evidence of widespread, documented community
concern—one of the routing criteria the Commission must weigh under PURA §
37.056(c).

E. Exhibits Should Be Admitted for a Limited, Non-Hearsay Purpose

Even if the exhibits are considered hearsay for purposes of proving scientific causation,
SOAH proceedings are administrative hearings, not civil jury trials. Administrative Law
Judges have discretion to admit hearsay evidence if it has probative value and is of a type
that reasonable people rely on.

I respectfully request that Exhibits AC-2 through AC-4 be admitted for the limited
purpose of:

   •   showing that these materials exist and are publicly available from major health
       institutions;
   •   demonstrating the basis for my state of mind and personal concern as a
       community member; and
   •   reflecting the current state of public information that shapes community values
       and public perception.

The Administrative Law Judges can assign whatever weight they deem appropriate,
rather than striking the exhibits entirely.



F. Request for Official Notice of IARC Classification

                                                                            Page 5|6
 I further request that the Administrative Law Judges take official notice of the fact that
the International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies extremely low frequency
(ELF) magnetic fields as Group 2B—“possibly carcinogenic to humans.”

This request does not ask the Commission to find that ELF fields cause cancer. It simply
asks recognition that this public health classification exists, is publicly available, and is
one of the reasons residents like me experience concern about living near a 765-kV
transmission line.

G. Route-Specific EMF Information Should Be Provided by Applicants

Rather than placing the burden on individual residents to prove or disprove EMF effects,
it is reasonable to require Applicants—who possess the engineering resources—to
provide route-specific EMF modeling and disclosure for affected residential areas before
any route is approved near homes and schools.

I am not claiming to know what the EMF levels will be. I am requesting that, before
approving a route near homes, schools, and a disabled veteran’s residence, the
Commission require Applicants to provide that information so that routing decisions can
be made with greater transparency and awareness.

                                  IV. CONCLUSION

For these reasons, I respectfully request that the Administrative Law Judges:

   1. Deny Applicants’ request to strike the challenged portions of my testimony and
      Exhibits AC-2 through AC-4;
   2. Alternatively, permit the exhibits to remain in the record for the limited purpose
      of demonstrating community concern, public awareness, and the basis for my
      personal concerns; and
   3. Consider requiring route-specific EMF modeling and disclosure for residential
      and school areas along any proposed route near Salado.

Respectfully submitted,

April Ciano
Pro Se Intervenor
